title: [RPG Design Guides] Dungeon Balance ③ Placement of Rest Points

blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】ダンジョンバランス③ 休憩地点の配置
blocks.translation: [RPG Design Guides] Dungeon Balance ③ Placement of Rest Points

blocks.source: ※ここで使用する「休憩地点」とは、ダンジョンの途中で「回復」と「セーブ」の両方ができる場所のこと。（「回復」はできるが「セーブ」はできない等のパターンも時々あるが、ここでは話を単純にするため上の様に定義する。）
blocks.translation: ※Here, a “rest point” means a location partway through a dungeon where both recovery and saving are possible. (There are also occasional variations where recovery is possible but saving is not; however, to keep things simple, it is defined as above here.)

blocks.source: ダンジョンの途中――特にボス戦前に休憩地点を「用意するか？」「用意しないか？」というのは悩ましい問題となる。
blocks.translation: Whether to “provide” or “not provide” a rest point partway through a dungeon—especially before a boss battle—is a difficult question.

blocks.source: ■休憩地点を用意した場合
blocks.translation: ■Advantages and Disadvantages of Providing a Rest Point

blocks.source: ダンジョン攻略中にザコ敵との戦闘でＨＰやＭＰを消耗しても、ボス戦前には、回復することができる。つまり、「ダンジョン＆ザコ戦」と「ボス戦」は別物であり、２つに分けて攻略できる。
blocks.translation: Even if the party’s HP and MP are depleted in battles against regular enemies while exploring the dungeon, they can recover before the boss battle. In other words, the “dungeon and regular battles” and the “boss battle” are separate, allowing players to tackle them independently.

blocks.source: ■休憩地点を用意しない場合
blocks.translation: ■Advantages and Disadvantages of Not Providing a Rest Point

blocks.source: ダンジョン攻略中にザコ敵との戦闘で消耗した場合、そのままの状態で、ボスに挑まなければならない。つまり、「ダンジョン」「ザコ戦」「ボス戦」の３つを合わせて攻略する必要がある。
blocks.translation: If the party is depleted in battles against regular enemies while exploring the dungeon, they must challenge the boss in that condition. In other words, the “dungeon,” “regular battles,” and “boss battle” must all be tackled together.

blocks.source: どちらが絶対に良いかとまでは言えないが、一般的には休憩地点を用意する方がお勧め。その理由を以下に細かく
blocks.translation: It is impossible to say that one option is absolutely better, but generally, I recommend providing a rest point. The reasons are explained below in detail, covering the

blocks.source: 「利点（青字）」
blocks.translation: advantages (in blue)

blocks.source: 「欠点（赤字）」
blocks.translation: and disadvantages (in red)

blocks.source: を述べながら説明する。
blocks.translation: as I explain them.

blocks.source: ■休憩地点を用意した場合の「利点」「欠点」
blocks.translation: ■Advantages and Disadvantages of Providing a Rest Point

blocks.source: プレイヤーが気軽にダンジョン探索ができる。ダンジョンを長めに設定しても安心。
blocks.translation: Players can explore the dungeon casually. Even if the dungeon is made fairly long, there is less cause for concern.

blocks.source: ザコ戦で遠慮なく魔法・特技を使用できる。つまり、ザコ敵を強く設定できる。
blocks.translation: Players can freely use magic and Techs in regular battles. In other words, regular enemies can be made stronger.

blocks.source: ボス戦でプレイヤーが全力を出せる。つまり、ボス敵を強く設定できる。
blocks.translation: Players can give their all in the boss battle. In other words, the boss can be made stronger.

blocks.source: プレイヤーを消耗させる意味でのザコ戦の意義がなくなる。
blocks.translation: Regular battles lose their purpose as a means of wearing down the player.

blocks.source: ■休憩地点を用意しない場合の「利点」「欠点」
blocks.translation: ■Advantages and Disadvantages of Not Providing a Rest Point

blocks.source: 「ダンジョン」「ザコ戦」「ボス戦」の３つを考慮する必要があるため、パーティの消耗に配慮した総合的な攻略をプレイヤーに要求できる。
blocks.translation: Since players must take the “dungeon,” “regular battles,” and “boss battle” into consideration, they can be required to develop an overall strategy that accounts for party depletion.

blocks.source: 一度でダンジョンをクリアすることが難しいので、複数回に分けて挑戦させたい場合に有効。
blocks.translation: This is effective when you want players to attempt the dungeon over multiple runs, since clearing it in a single attempt is difficult.

blocks.source: 気軽にダンジョン探索できない。（せっかく作ったダンジョンが･･･）
blocks.translation: Players cannot explore the dungeon casually. (What a shame for the dungeon you worked so hard to create...)

blocks.source: ザコ戦で消耗を控えるため、地味になりやすい。
blocks.translation: Because players need to avoid depletion in regular battles, the experience is likely to become subdued.

blocks.source: ザコ戦で消耗を控えるため、町の周囲でパーティを強化し、ダンジョン内の戦闘では「逃げる」を多用するというプレイスタイルを推奨してしまう。（せっかく作ったダンジョン内のザコ敵が･･･）
blocks.translation: To avoid depletion in regular battles, players may strengthen their party around town and adopt a play style that frequently uses “Escape” during battles inside the dungeon. (What a shame for the regular enemies you worked so hard to place in the dungeon...)

blocks.source: という具合に「休憩地点を用意した場合」の方が欠点が少なく、利点が多くあると思える。
blocks.translation: Thus, it seems that “providing a rest point” has more advantages and fewer disadvantages.

blocks.source: また、難易度という観点から見ると、何となく、
blocks.translation: Also, from a difficulty perspective, one might get the impression that

blocks.source: 休憩地点を用意する → ライトユーザ向け
blocks.translation: Providing a rest point → for light users

blocks.source: 休憩地点を用意しない → ヘビーユーザ向け
blocks.translation: Not providing a rest point → for heavy users

blocks.source: という印象を持ってしまいそうだけど、こうして見ると「休憩地点を用意する場合」でも、戦闘を激しくできる等、ヘビーユーザが好む要素も備えていることが分かるはず。
blocks.translation: but looking at it this way, even “providing a rest point” includes elements that heavy users enjoy, such as allowing battles to be made more intense.

blocks.source: 「休憩地点を用意しない場合」の「利点」として
blocks.translation: As an “advantage” of “not providing a rest point,”

blocks.source: 「ダンジョン」「ザコ戦」「ボス戦」の３つを考慮する必要があるため、パーティの消耗に配慮した総合的な攻略をプレイヤーに要求できる。
blocks.translation: since players must take the “dungeon,” “regular battles,” and “boss battle” into consideration, they can be required to develop an overall strategy that accounts for party depletion.

blocks.source: と記述したけど、逆に言えば
blocks.translation: I described it that way, but conversely,

blocks.source: 「ダンジョンの長さ」「ザコ敵の強さ」「ボス敵の強さ」といった情報を持たない限り正確な攻略は立てられないということになる。これは「攻略情報を知らないプレイヤー」にとっては厳しい条件。
blocks.translation: it means that players cannot devise an accurate strategy unless they have information such as the “dungeon’s length,” “regular enemies’ strength,” and “boss’s strength.” This is a harsh condition for players who do not have walkthrough information.

blocks.source: ダンジョンをクリアする前に、攻略情報を知るには、
blocks.translation: To learn the necessary walkthrough information before clearing the dungeon, players must

blocks.source: 攻略本や攻略サイトに頼る。
blocks.translation: rely on a strategy guide or walkthrough site.

blocks.source: 一度ダンジョンに挑戦して、途中で引き返す。または全滅してやり直す。
blocks.translation: attempt the dungeon once and turn back partway through, or get wiped out and try again.

blocks.source: などの方法が必要となる。
blocks.translation: Methods such as these are necessary.

blocks.source: 間違いなくこれはライトユーザにとっては厳しいし、ヘビーユーザでもこの様に時間のかかるバランス調整を好まない人も多いと思う。（※攻略本・攻略サイトは利用しないことを前提にしてます。）
blocks.translation: There is no doubt that this is harsh for light users, and I think many heavy users also dislike balance adjustments that require this much time. (※This assumes that players will not use strategy guides or walkthrough sites.)

blocks.source: 制作者はプレイヤーが攻略情報を知らないという前提で調整すべき
blocks.translation: Considering that creators should balance the game assuming that players do not have walkthrough information,

blocks.source: ということを考えると、調整がいかに難しいかわかると思う。
blocks.translation: I think you can see how difficult the balancing process is.

blocks.source: さらに言えば、「休憩地点を用意しない場合」は特に
blocks.translation: Furthermore, when “not providing a rest point,” you must be especially

blocks.source: テストプレイ時には「製作者」と「プレイヤー」との間の攻略情報の差に気を付けなければならない。
blocks.translation: careful during test play about the difference in walkthrough information between the “creator” and the “player.”

blocks.source: というのも「ダンジョンの長さ」などの情報は知っているか知らないかで、ダンジョン攻略時の心理的負担が大きく異なるから。制作者がテストプレイヤーをする時には、無意識の内に攻略情報を前提としたバランス調整をしないように注意しなければならない。
blocks.translation: This is because knowing or not knowing information such as the “dungeon’s length” greatly affects the psychological burden of exploring the dungeon. When creators test-play their own games, they must be careful not to unconsciously balance the game based on walkthrough information.

blocks.source: 「休憩地点を用意した場合」ならば、その点の懸念は軽減される。「ダンジョン＆ザコ戦」をくぐり抜ければ、「ボス戦」前に一旦、回復できるため、それぞれを別個にバランス調整できることが大きい。
blocks.translation: If “a rest point is provided,” this concern is reduced. Once players make it through the “dungeon and regular battles,” they can recover before the “boss battle,” making it possible to balance each part separately.

blocks.source: 以上より、
blocks.translation: Therefore,

blocks.source: 休憩地点を用意する → ライトユーザにもヘビーユーザにもお勧め
blocks.translation: Providing a rest point → recommended for both light and heavy users

blocks.source: 休憩地点を用意しない → ヘビーユーザ専用
blocks.translation: Not providing a rest point → for heavy users only

blocks.source: 「休憩地点を用意する」方がより広い層を取り込めるんじゃないかなと。
blocks.translation: I think “providing a rest point” can appeal to a broader range of players.

blocks.source: もっとも「休憩地点を用意しない場合」でも、複数回に分けて、ダンジョンを攻略させたい時には有効となることもある。
blocks.translation: That said, even “not providing a rest point” can be effective when you want players to tackle a dungeon over multiple attempts.

blocks.source: 例えば、ペルソナ４には、
blocks.translation: For example, Persona 4 has

blocks.source: ・仲間との交友などを楽しむ日常パート
blocks.translation: ・everyday segments where players enjoy socializing with their companions

blocks.source: ・探索や戦闘を楽しむダンジョンパート
blocks.translation: ・dungeon segments where players enjoy exploration and battles

blocks.source: の２つのパートがある。
blocks.translation: has two parts.

blocks.source: ダンジョンパートでは、１ダンジョンが長めであるにも関わらず、休憩地点がない、または
blocks.translation: In the dungeon sections, despite each dungeon being fairly long, there are no rest areas, or

blocks.source: 回復に多額の金が必要。
blocks.translation: healing costs a lot.

blocks.source: という調整をしているため、パーティが消耗した場合、必然的にダンジョンパートを途中で中断して、日常パートに戻らなくてはならなくなる。
blocks.translation: Because I have made this adjustment, when the party becomes worn out, they inevitably have to interrupt the dungeon section midway and return to the daily-life section.

blocks.source: （※実は後半はたくさんお金が入るので、いつまでもダンジョンに潜れたり……）
blocks.translation: (※ In fact, since you receive a lot of money in the latter half, you can stay in dungeons indefinitely...)

blocks.source: けれど、それによってプレイヤーは自然とダンジョンパートと日常パートを交互に行うという、制作者の意図に沿ったプレイをするようになっている。
blocks.translation: However, this naturally leads players to play in accordance with the creator's intentions, alternating between the dungeon and daily-life sections.

blocks.source: ダンジョンの攻略ぐらいしか、やることが無い一本道のゲームで同じような調整をすると、単にテンポが悪くなるだけで、不評を買いそうだけど、他の要素との兼ね合い次第では、あえて「休憩地点を用意しない場合」のもありだと思う。
blocks.translation: In a linear game where there is little to do besides clearing dungeons, making the same adjustment would merely hurt the pacing and likely draw criticism. However, depending on how it fits with the other elements, I think there are cases where deliberately “not providing rest areas” is a valid option.

blocks.source: 先程、
blocks.translation: Earlier,

blocks.source: 回復に多額の金が必要
blocks.translation: healing costs a lot

blocks.source: という文章をさりげなく強調してみたが、このように、ダンジョン内に多額の金などの条件を課した休憩地点を配置するのは、「休憩地点を用意する場合」「休憩地点を用意しない場合」の中間策となる。
blocks.translation: I subtly emphasized the phrase, but placing rest areas in dungeons with conditions such as requiring a large sum of money, as in this example, is a middle-ground approach between “providing rest areas” and “not providing rest areas.”

blocks.source: 例えば……
blocks.translation: For example...

blocks.source: あまりに、回復が簡単すぎると、休憩地点周辺で、経験値稼ぎをする場合に「消費を気にせず全力でザコ戦」→「終了後、即回復」を延々と繰り返す――のような、機械的なプレイを推奨してしまうことになり兼ねない。
blocks.translation: If healing is too easy, when players are grinding for experience around a rest area, it could end up encouraging mechanical play, such as endlessly repeating “fight trash mobs at full strength without worrying about resource consumption” → “heal immediately after finishing.”

blocks.source: 別にそれでも問題ないような気がしないでもないけど、僕個人的には適度に町の宿屋に泊まりながら稼ぐ方が好きです。何となく、その方が温かみが感じられるので……。
blocks.translation: I can't say that would necessarily be a problem, but personally, I prefer earning money while staying at inns in town from time to time. Somehow, that feels warmer...

blocks.source: ・また、「上手に消耗を避けて戦ったプレイヤー」と「下手に消耗して戦ったプレイヤー」とで、回復にかかる料金で待遇を差別化したい。
blocks.translation: ・I also want to differentiate the treatment of players who skillfully avoided exhaustion in battle from those who became exhausted through poor play, by charging them different healing fees.

blocks.source: ・回復には何らかの制約を設けたいが、回復が全くできないのは苦しすぎるし、やはり、ボス戦では万全の状態で、戦って欲しい。
blocks.translation: ・I want to place some kind of restriction on healing, but being unable to heal at all would be too harsh. Besides, I want players to fight bosses in perfect condition.

blocks.source: などの場合には、この中間策もお勧め。
blocks.translation: In cases like these, this middle-ground approach is also recommended.

blocks.source: 何はともあれ、どの様に休憩地点を「用意する」「用意しない」にしても、なぜ、その作品ではそうしているのか？自分なりに、筋を通して説明できるようにしたい。
blocks.translation: In any case, whether you “provide” rest areas or “do not provide” them, I want to be able to explain coherently, in my own way, why I chose that approach for the work in question.

texts.もっとも「休憩地点を用意しない場合」でも、複数回に分けて、ダンジョンを攻略させた: That said, even “not providing a rest point” can be effective when you want players to tackle a dungeon over multiple attempts.
texts.・仲間との交友などを楽しむ日常パート: ・everyday segments where players enjoy socializing with their companions
texts.・探索や戦闘を楽しむダンジョンパート: ・dungeon segments where players enjoy exploration and battles
texts.ダンジョンパートでは、１ダンジョンが長めであるにも関わらず、休憩地点がない、また: In the dungeon sections, despite each dungeon being fairly long, there are no rest areas, or
texts.という調整をしているため、パーティが消耗した場合、必然的にダンジョンパートを途中: Because I have made this adjustment, when the party becomes worn out, they inevitably have to interrupt the dungeon section midway and return to the daily-life section.
texts.（※実は後半はたくさんお金が入るので、いつまでもダンジョンに潜れたり……）: (※ In fact, since you receive a lot of money in the latter half, you can stay in dungeons indefinitely...)
texts.けれど、それによってプレイヤーは自然とダンジョンパートと日常パートを交互に行うと: However, this naturally leads players to play in accordance with the creator's intentions, alternating between the dungeon and daily-life sections.
texts.ダンジョンの攻略ぐらいしか、やることが無い一本道のゲームで同じような調整をすると: In a linear game where there is little to do besides clearing dungeons, making the same adjustment would merely hurt the pacing and likely draw criticism. However, depending on how it fits with the other elements, I think there are cases where deliberately “not providing rest areas” is a valid option.
texts.という文章をさりげなく強調してみたが、このように、ダンジョン内に多額の金などの条: I subtly emphasized the phrase, but placing rest areas in dungeons with conditions such as requiring a large sum of money, as in this example, is a middle-ground approach between “providing rest areas” and “not providing rest areas.”
texts.あまりに、回復が簡単すぎると、休憩地点周辺で、経験値稼ぎをする場合に「消費を気に: If healing is too easy, when players are grinding for experience around a rest area, it could end up encouraging mechanical play, such as endlessly repeating “fight trash mobs at full strength without worrying about resource consumption” → “heal immediately after finishing.”
texts.別にそれでも問題ないような気がしないでもないけど、僕個人的には適度に町の宿屋に泊: I can't say that would necessarily be a problem, but personally, I prefer earning money while staying at inns in town from time to time. Somehow, that feels warmer...
texts.・また、「上手に消耗を避けて戦ったプレイヤー」と「下手に消耗して戦ったプレイヤー: ・I also want to differentiate the treatment of players who skillfully avoided exhaustion in battle from those who became exhausted through poor play, by charging them different healing fees.
texts.・回復には何らかの制約を設けたいが、回復が全くできないのは苦しすぎるし、やはり、: ・I want to place some kind of restriction on healing, but being unable to heal at all would be too harsh. Besides, I want players to fight bosses in perfect condition.
texts.などの場合には、この中間策もお勧め。: In cases like these, this middle-ground approach is also recommended.
texts.何はともあれ、どの様に休憩地点を「用意する」「用意しない」にしても、なぜ、その作: In any case, whether you “provide” rest areas or “do not provide” them, I want to be able to explain coherently, in my own way, why I chose that approach for the work in question.
